facts.claim: Visit Greece (the official Greek tourism site) says Santorini, known in ancient times as Thera, is at the southernmost point of the Cyclades and comprises a complex of islands: Thera, Thirasia, Aspronisi, Palea Kameni and Nea Kameni. It says the island owes its fame to its active volcano, in whose caldera you can stay, and that hamlets spread across the rim of the caldera.

Visit Greece describes Santorini's beaches as black, red and white sand, multicoloured pebbles and steep cliffs, and says the island is arid with fertile soil, mainly growing vines, yellow split peas and tomatoes. The page names no individual villages (Oia, Fira, Imerovigli and Pyrgos are not named on the page as read).

Visit Greece lists flights from Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) to Santorini Airport with a travel duration of 50 minutes, and from Thessaloniki Airport (Macedonia) to Santorini Airport of 1 hour and 30 minutes (scheduled durations stated by the tourism board). The page as read gives no ferry route or crossing time from Piraeus.

The official website of Santorini Airport (JTR), served through Fraport Greece's airport systems, lists airlines serving the airport including Aegean Airlines, Olympic Air and Sky Express alongside European and Gulf carriers such as British Airways, Lufthansa, Qatar Airways, Etihad Airways, Gulf Air and FlyDubai, and has Schengen and non-Schengen departure areas. It lists ways to and from the airport by public bus and by taxi, and has an Accessible Travel section for passengers with reduced mobility.

Visit Greece (official Greek tourism site, read live 11 November 2026) describes Mykonos as 'the island of the winds', in the heart of the Cyclades, synonymous with cosmopolitanism and luxurious holidays, with paved streets, white houses, chapels, dry-stone walls and windmills, beaches it calls among the most beautiful in the Aegean, its Hora, the Little Venice neighbourhood with houses built against the sea, and the windmills as the island's trademark.

Visit Greece (read live 11 November 2026) lists flights from Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) to Mykonos Airport of about 45 minutes and from Thessaloniki Airport (Macedonia) of about 1 hour 10 minutes. The page does not name the meltemi or give seasonal wind data, and it gives no ferry or port details.

Mykonos Airport's official website ('The official website of Mykonos Airport (JMK)', read live 11 November 2026) is run within the Fraport Greece network (it links to 'Fraport Greece's plans for the new airport'). Its 'To and From the Airport' section lists GPS location information, a direct public bus service to and from the airport, and taxis; it also lists accessible travel information for passengers with reduced mobility, parking, border control and a Private Flights Lounge with VIP welcoming services.

Mykonos Airport's official site says a bus service runs between the airport and the city of Mykonos (Chora) and other destinations, from a stop in front of the terminal building (Arrivals area), with tickets bought from the driver (more information at mykonosbus.com); a taxi stand is outside the Arrivals terminal building.

Canaves Collection (Oia) Weddings page: 'Panorama Balcony – Canaves Oia Suites ... up to 30 guests can gather as the stunning Caldera and the endless Aegean set the scene for an impeccable wedding ceremony.' CALDERA WORDING: 'the stunning Caldera and the endless Aegean set the scene'.

Canaves Collection wedding enquiry form lists ceremony types Religious, Civil, Symbolic and Vow Renewal; the page says it caters 'from traditional weddings to modern elopements' and links a wedding brochure with package options (no amounts recorded).

Grace Hotel Santorini (Auberge Resorts Collection) is in Imerovigli, Santorini; its Weddings page describes a 'dramatic cliffside location' and 'intimate scale', perched on a clifftop above the Aegean, with ceremonies 363 metres above sea level facing caldera sunsets. Venue type: cliff-top suite hotel.
Grace Hotel offers a unity ceremony in which the couple combine black and white volcanic sand collected from Santorini beaches.

Santo Wines (the winery of the Union of Santorini Cooperatives) is in Pyrgos, Santorini; its Wine Tourism Center sits next to the winery with a volcano view and is open all year round. Venue type: winery.
Santo Wines has a dedicated Weddings page under 'Host your event' and says it 'provides a stunning backdrop for couples', describing saying 'I do' with the caldera as witness against the setting sun.

Katikies Hotels list Santorini properties Katikies Santorini (Pelagos House and Gea House, Oia), Katikies Chromata (Imerovigli) and Katikies Garden (Fira); the Events page names Weddings and 'Hotel Take over' among event types.

Katikies Santorini (Oia): Botrini's Restaurant seated 60 / standing 100, described as ideal for wedding ceremonies, lunches, dinners and standing cocktail receptions; Katikies Lounge Lower Deck seated 50 / standing 100.

Andronis Weddings & Celebrations page: 'Picture yourselves exchanging vows against the awe-inspiring caldera, as the sun dips into the horizon'; enquiry form event types Wedding, Birthday, Anniversary, Dining Event; a wedding brochure is linked. The page does not name which Andronis property hosts ceremonies, and notes it contains 'materials generated using AI'. CALDERA WORDING: 'exchanging vows against the awe-inspiring caldera'.

Andronis Luxury Suites (Oia): '39 acclaimed suites and villas ... Perched atop cliffs, they offer mesmerizing views of the Aegean Sea against the volcanic caldera'; home to Lycabettus Restaurant (described as Greece's only 2-MICHELIN Starred) and Mare Sanus Spa. The hotel page menu links to the group Weddings & Celebrations page.

Grand Ambassador Santorini (home page) describes itself as 'a luxurious haven perched on the cliffs of Akrotiri', offering 'breathtaking caldera views and the iconic Santorini volcano as your daily backdrop'. It lists 40 private pools and its suites are titled with 'Caldera View'.

Grand Ambassador's venue page says it hosts proposals, weddings, honeymoons and anniversaries, with 'over 700 square meters of elegant outdoor space accommodating up to 250 guests'. Couples may choose a favourite available pool for a private photo session.

Grand Ambassador's venue page says it offers Wedding and Honeymoon Packages, and that couples can work with their own wedding planner or with the hotel's concierge team. Enquiries go to its events team.

Santa Marina's home page structured data describes it as 'a beachfront retreat on a private peninsula at the southern tip of Ornos Bay, Mykonos', with rooms, suites and villas with Aegean views, infinity pools, a private sandy beach and the Ginkgo Spa, 'just minutes from Mykonos Town'; the resort is marking 40 years. It does not use the word 'Cycladic' on the pages read.

Santa Marina's own 'Weddings & Celebrations' page (live, modified 23 October 2026) says the resort sits 'on the pristine shores of Mykonos', that its venues have 'scenic panoramas of the Aegean Sea', and that it has a 'traditional whitewashed stone chapel'. Re-check of Greece venues pack fact_10, fact_11: unchanged in substance.

Santa Marina says its 'experienced team of wedding planners' works with couples on intimate gatherings or grand celebrations, including bespoke menus, floral arrangements and elopement parties, and publishes a 2026 wedding brochure PDF and event menus PDF. Capacity, room count and exclusive use are not stated on the page read.

Mykonos Grand Hotel & Resort describes itself as a five-star beachfront hotel on Ayios Yiannis (Agios Ioannis) beach, opposite the island of Delos, a member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World, with a private beach section reserved for hotel guests. Its home page meta description mentions 'Cycladic charm'.

Mykonos Grand's weddings page says its whitewashed chapel dedicated to the Virgin Mary is 'perched on a hill looking out over Ayios Yiannis Beach'; it holds up to 25 guests indoors and serves as a backdrop for outdoor ceremonies for up to 100 guests. The hotel will liaise with the couple's wedding planner and arranges music, video and photography, beauty salon services and flowers.

Mykonos Grand states that both bride and groom must be Christian Orthodox to perform a (religious) wedding within the hotel premises. Its amenity list also names an open-air amphitheatre and a complimentary evening shuttle to Mykonos Town. Accommodation includes rooms, suites with private pools and the Mykonos Grand Villa; total room count and exclusive use are not stated on the pages read.

Mykonos Blu (Grecotel) has a live 'Weddings & Vow Renewals' page (modified 21 October 2026) offering wedding experiences on Psarou beach with the sunset as a backdrop. Venue type: 5-star beachfront hotel described as a Cycladic settlement on the waterfront, with 103 guest rooms.

Mykonos Blu ceremony option as stated: The Ocean Balcony, accommodating up to 60 guests, perched just above Psarou beach with an uninterrupted sea view. After the ceremony the hotel can arrange a wedding table and party for up to 120 guests in its L'Archipel restaurant and pool area. Exclusive use is not published.

Saint John Hotel Villas & Spa has a live weddings page saying it 'offers a variety of wedding venues and event spaces', located in Agios Ioannis, which it calls one of Mykonos' most iconic sunset spots. Venue type: hotel, villas and spa resort.

Saint John ceremony and reception options as stated: vows at Agia Fotini Chapel, the sunset balcony or the deck; receptions at Theatraki, 1001 Nights, Ilios or Thalatta (the page calls these ideal for indoor wedding venues). All venues are described as having full sea views.

Katikies Mykonos describes itself as a 5-star hotel and member of The Leading Hotels of the World 'above the sun kissed beach of Agios Ioannis', about 4 km from Mykonos Town (about a 10-minute drive); all rooms and suites look to Agios Ioannis beach and most have sea views to Delos; children above 13 are welcome (younger children are directed to sister property Katikies Villas Mykonos at Elia beach). Room count is not stated on the page read.

Katikies events page lists four Katikies Mykonos venues: Upper deck (seated 50, standing 100, 'Ideal for wedding ceremonies; private dinners; standing cocktail receptions'); Botrini's Restaurant (seated 50, standing 60); Fleur de Miraval (seated 50, standing 80); Private Balcony (seated 20, standing 20). Only the Upper deck is marked for wedding ceremonies.

Myconian Collection's weddings page (re-read live, modified 28 September 2026) says couples can exchange vows in a small whitewashed chapel followed by a reception on the beach or in one of its restaurants overlooking the Aegean and Mykonos town; it names its hotels in Elia as the wedding hotels and says it can prepare the stage for the couple's own team or provide a complete event solution (invitations, travel logistics, VIP transportation, menus, specialist cakes, wines, flowers, favours, lighting, sound and music, honeymoon planning) and fireworks over the bay. Re-confirms greece-wedding-venues fact_12 and greece-wedding-packages fact_25.

Myconian Collection says it assists in officiating ceremonies across all denominations, has certified halal and kosher kitchens and a South Asian chef for traditional Indian cuisine, and its chefs' work has earned four Relais & Chateaux accolades; its guest transfer fleet includes luxury limousines, Porsche Cayennes, Mercedes 15-seat limo minibuses and 40-seat limo mini-coaches, with private jet, helicopter and yacht services on request. Re-confirms greece-wedding-venues fact_14 (Porsche Cayennes now also listed).
facts.conflicts: Transfer fleet now also lists Porsche Cayennes; greece-wedding-venues fact_14 listed limousines, minibuses and mini-coaches only. No numeric conflict.

facts.claim: Myconian Ambassador official homepage: 'Set above Platis Gialos beach ... just 5km away from the vibrant energy of Mykonos Town', with neighbouring Psarou within walking distance. It lists Weddings & events among its services ('As experts in romance and discretion...') and its fine-dining restaurant Efisia. Room count is not stated on the pages read. The hotel is part of the Myconian Collection.

Grecotel Mykonos Lolita's own weddings page (grecotel.com/mykonos-lolita/weddings-mykonos/, modified 22 July 2026) offers 'Religious, civil & symbolic weddings at the hotel's chapel overlooking the deep blue and crystal-clear waters', describes the setting as off the beaten path and close to the island of Delos, and takes enquiries through a request-for-proposal form and the hotel's events email.

The Hellenic National Meteorological Service (HNMS/EMY) 'Climatic Data by City' page has no Santorini (Thira) station; for the South Aegean it lists only Naxos and Rodos. Naxos is the nearest listed station and any figures must be labelled as Naxos, not Santorini.

The Hellenic National Meteorological Service (HNMS/EMY) 'Climatic Data for selected stations in Greece' page, requested for Mykonos in the South Aegean and read live 11 November 2026, lists only Naxos and Rodos as stations for the South Aegean and returns no Mykonos table, so no monthly temperature, rainfall, rain-day or wind data for a Mykonos station was available from this page.
facts.conflicts: Conflicts with the brief note that a Mykonos station exists on this page; the venues pack fact_307 recorded the same absence.

facts.claim: HNMS Naxos station (lon 25.369, lat 37.081, altitude 3 m; the page states 'Data Period: None') shows monthly mean temperatures of 16.1 C in April, 19.6 C in May, 23.5 C in June, 25.1 C in July, 25.0 C in August, 23.0 C in September and 19.7 C in October. Mean maximum temperatures are 18.7, 22.1, 25.9, 27.1, 27.0, 25.1 and 21.9 C for the same months.

HNMS Naxos station shows monthly mean precipitation of 17.6 mm in April, 10.6 mm in May, 2.4 mm in June, 0.9 mm in July, 1.6 mm in August, 7.7 mm in September and 38.6 mm in October, with mean precipitation days of 6.0, 3.6, 1.1, 0.4, 0.3, 1.9 and 5.5 respectively.

HNMS Naxos station shows a prevailing wind direction of north in every month, with monthly mean wind power of 11.7 in April, 10.0 in May, 10.3 in June, 13.3 in July, 13.8 in August, 13.9 in September and 14.5 in October (units not stated on the page).

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's overall advice for Greece is 'Exercise normal safety precautions' (level green); the page was updated 30 September 2026 and shows 'still current at 12 November 2026' when read on 11 November 2026 (Australian date).

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says heatwaves are frequent over the summer months (drink plenty of water, wear light clothing, stay in air conditioning or shade, follow local authorities), and that wildfires occur during the extended summer period from June to September, including near cities and tourist locations, prompting evacuations; fires can start with little warning and travel quickly. Expect travel disruptions in areas that might be affected.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says wildfires occur in Greece during the extended summer period, from June to September, including near cities and tourist locations, prompting evacuations; fires can start with little warning and travel quickly. Extreme weather can affect Greece throughout the year, including heavy snowfall and flooding in winter.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says during the May to October tourist season to be prepared for high temperatures and large crowds at popular seaports; in most cases you will carry luggage up and down stairs on ferries; ferry services can be delayed or cancelled in bad weather, mainly due to strong winds, so check the forecast and reconfirm departures. It says on some Greek islands, such as Santorini, smaller boats or tenders carry cruise ship passengers to and from shore and passengers using tenders may have difficulty with stairs.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says ferries and large catamarans carry most visitors to the Greek islands; some services lack suitable access for people with disabilities, and in most cases you carry luggage up and down stairs (help is usually unavailable unless you have booked a private cabin). During the tourist season, May to October, expect high temperatures and large crowds at popular seaports. Ferry services can be delayed or cancelled in bad weather, mainly due to strong winds, so check the forecast and reconfirm departures with your travel provider.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says Greece is in an active seismic zone and experiences earthquakes and volcanic activity, including near major tourist destinations such as Santorini and Crete; monitor the media and follow local authorities' advice.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says Greece is in the Schengen area; Australians can make short trips without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and on arrival for a short stay on an Australian passport you register biometric details (fingerprints and a photo) under the European Entry/Exit System (EES), which has no cost and needs no action before arrival, though there may be delays at border crossings. Depending on why you travel and how long you stay you may need a visa, and entry conditions can change at short notice, so contact the nearest embassy or consulate. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says same-sex relationships are legal in Greece though attitudes vary; avoid public displays of affection, especially in rural areas; attitudes are generally more accepting on islands such as Mykonos, Santorini and Ios. The page does not address same-sex civil marriage.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's 'Getting married overseas' page (last updated 18/08/2026, read live 11 November 2026) says some countries ask you to prove you are not already married, and each country decides what proof it accepts; the most common documents are a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and certificates from a registry of births, deaths and marriages (a statement of no record of a previous marriage, a Single Status certificate or a No Record Result certificate). Local authorities may also ask for divorce papers, a deceased spouse's death certificate, and your original birth certificate and passport. There may be different regional and national laws, so contact the destination's embassy or consulate for specific details. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller (read live 11 November 2026) says DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their country, so ask the destination's embassy or consulate whether you need a CNI, whether you can get it in Australia, and whether it also needs an authentication or apostille. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller (read live 11 November 2026) says you cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if, when it took place, it was valid under the law of the country where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law had it occurred in Australia. A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage but may not work as proof of a name change (check with your local registry of births, deaths and marriages), and Smartraveller suggests talking to a lawyer to confirm the certificate is valid in Australia. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller (read live 11 November 2026) says Australia does not recognise overseas marriages where one or both people are already married to someone else, not old enough to marry, too closely related, or forced to marry.

As at November 2026, the Australian Embassy in Athens notarial services page (read live 11 November 2026) lists witnessing application forms for, and issuing, Certificates of No Impediment (CNI), witnessing notices of intended marriage, and legalisation of signatures and/or seals by authentication or apostille. An appointment is needed for all notarial services (Monday to Friday, 9:00am to 12:30pm), though apostille and CNI documents can be submitted by post; legalised (apostilled) documents and CNIs are available for collection within two working days unless same-day collection is arranged in advance, or can be returned by mail. A fee applies. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, the Australian Embassy in Athens (read live 11 November 2026) says it does not provide legal advice, the client is responsible for knowing which service they need, it does not witness signatures on overseas documents (ask local authorities who can witness, or get legal advice), and honorary consuls are not authorised to provide notarial services.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's 'How to get your documents legalised' (last updated 30/09/2026, read live 11 November 2026) says to ask the overseas authority which documents they need and which must be legalised (DFAT cannot tell you what they may want), and to find out from the intended authority or legal representative whether you need an apostille or an authentication certificate. Documents that are not original Australian public documents must first be notarised by an Australian Notary Public. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller (read live 11 November 2026) says legalisation processing times vary, with delays when demand rises at the end of the school year and in peak holiday periods, for incomplete requests or unpaid fees, or when the issuing authority must be contacted. An Australian-issued apostille can be verified online via DFAT.

insider_details.detail: Santorini's wedding setting is the caldera rim: Canaves (Oia), Grace (Imerovigli), Andronis (Oia), Santo Wines (Pyrgos) and Grand Ambassador (Akrotiri) all sell caldera or sunset views, while Mykonos venues sell beaches and bays (Psarou, Ornos, Agios Ioannis, Elia). Choose the island by whether the couple pictures a cliff-edge ceremony or a beachfront party.

Santorini's caldera ceremony spaces published by the venues are mostly small (Canaves Panorama Balcony up to 30; Grace intimate scale), with Grand Ambassador's 700 sq m outdoor space up to 250 the larger exception; on Mykonos, Mykonos Blu takes up to 60 for the ceremony and up to 120 for the party. Shortlist venues by guest count before falling for a view.

Ceremony type narrows the list on both islands: Canaves lists Religious, Civil, Symbolic and Vow Renewal; Grecotel Mykonos Lolita offers religious, civil and symbolic at its chapel; Mykonos Grand requires both partners to be Christian Orthodox for a religious wedding on site. Confirm the ceremony type before paying a venue deposit.

Plan for the same summer risks on either island: Smartraveller flags heatwaves and June to September wildfires, and says ferries can be delayed or cancelled in strong winds. Fly guests in (Athens to Santorini about 50 minutes, to Mykonos about 45 minutes per Visit Greece) and leave a buffer day before the wedding.

Climate figures can only be quoted for HNMS Naxos, which neither island has as its own station: Naxos averages under 1 mm of rain in July and August and a north wind in every month. Label any figure 'Naxos (nearest listed HNMS station)'.

Legal paperwork is identical whichever island you choose: a CNI and legalised documents via DFAT or the Australian Embassy in Athens (appointment needed), and the marriage is not registered in Australia but is usually recognised if valid in Greece. As at November 2026; the Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.
